quest.title: Truly Mouthwatering!
quest.description: You and Paimon are attracted by the aroma of roast chicken...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x15000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Thank you! Thank you! Thank you so much! You are my saviors! I, Henri, will never forget your kindness!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's focus on a more important matter. Paimon's curious how you ended up here.

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: *sigh* Those crabs must've been attracted here by the aroma of roast chicken.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon is attracted here by that, too!

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: No, that's different. Those crabs were probably choosing between me and the roast chicken as the starter. Just the thought that they might've chosen the "fresh starter" gives me chills.

choices.text: Sounds about right. The fresher, the better.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Paimon was asking about Henri, not the crabs! Who else would be buried in the ground!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, do you need help?

response.speaker: Henri
response.text: Naturally...

response.speaker: Henri
response.text: Um... No! I mean, no! Do not help me out!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Waah, okay, okay! We heard you, loud and clear! Let's go, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Henri
response.text: No, wait, please...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What's up?

response.speaker: Henri
response.text: I... I, uh... *ahem* Here's the thing. Please listen to me carefully. This, is a brand-new beauty fad!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You don't need to shout! Paimon's ears hurt!

response.speaker: Henri
response.text: Worry not! I am a perfectly sane person! I am adopting a beauty practice that is scientific and healthy! Which is why I buried myself in the moist sands with my own hands!

response.speaker: Henri
response.text: Please leave! Do not block my sunlight!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... Let's go...?

response.speaker: Henri
response.text: Since you're curious! Then you leave me with no choice but to explain the magic of this skincare treatment! Um, the clam worms in the sand can clear the...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #(Ugh, so loud. {NICKNAME}, what is up with this person? Paimon can't understand his words at all.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (This is really weird...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Is that so? What do you think?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Let's check the vicinity first.)

response.speaker: Henri
response.text: Eh? Are you leaving?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yes, we'll look around and come back later.

response.speaker: Henri
response.text: Okay! Off you go!

choices.text: I'm more curious about why you're buried in the ground...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, do you need help?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Don't leave Paimon in this awkward silence!

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: ...Hello.

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: What a beautiful day.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the person over there...

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: What person?

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: I don't know the person you're talking about.

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: We're just...

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: Taking a walk.

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: Yes, that's right. We are just taking a walk. A walk, taken by us, two totally ordinary people.

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: What a beautiful day and what a wonderful thing walking is! Don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: Taking a walk is totally normal. I'm sure you understand.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... What are you guys even talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did you hear someone calling for help? A man is buried in the ground over there and almost got eaten by crabs!

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: What? Something like that happened where we take walks?

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: On such a beautiful day?

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: If he gets eaten by crabs...

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: That'll be really funny. Uh, I mean, a real pity.

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: Shame, we won't let this happen. I mean, we can't let this happen.

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: If we run into something like this during our walk, we will not be bystanders. I mean, if.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What are you guys doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: Taking a walk.

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: Like we said, taking a walk.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You really didn't notice anything weird?

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: No, none at all.

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: Yeah, none at all. Except that the two of you are interrupting our walk.

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: Taking walks is... very personal. We do not like being interrupted.

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: We suggest that you find a good place for walks. The Fountain of Lucine, for instance, is a pretty good place.

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: This is where we take walks. I mean, where we feel the nature.

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: That's why we don't want to be interrupted. Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: Hello.

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: We are taking a walk.

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: And we hope that you will not interrupt our walk.

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: ...Don't doubt me! I buried myself with my very own hands! This is the latest beauty trend!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Uh... {NICKNAME}, any thoughts?

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: *sigh* I have done noth— I... This is the latest beauty trend...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Waah! When did you...

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: We are taking a walk. Taking walks... is a form of exercise.

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: Exercise involves movement. Movement is what brought us here.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Did you do this?

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: So what if...

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: #Oh, Hunter, I remember now. Take a good look at {M#him}{F#her}.

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: That's the person he told us not to mess with.

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: Right, right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you whispering about?

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: Nothing. We are just taking a walk.

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: That's right. We are just taking a walk. If there's nothing else, we'll...

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: Keep walking and walk to other places.

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Wait, don't you have to do anything scary to me anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: The lesson has been learned, if you know what I mean.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What lesson?

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: Nothing. I mean, roast chicken is dangerous. It invites trouble. See it as a valuable lesson. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Hunter
dialogues.text: But, roast chicken is... Debord...

dialogues.speaker: Turner
dialogues.text: Forget the roast chicken! We should continue our walk.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: "We'll ask Sonny to treat us to roast chicken next time."\nSo says Turner as he walks away with Hunter.

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Thank you! Thank you so much! I knew you'd understand!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Seems it is exactly like what {NICKNAME} said... Let's help Henri out!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But digging you out is a really exhausting job! So Paimon will take the roast chicken as payment!

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Huh? Ugh... Alright, fine!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: It takes you a while to help Henri out of the sands and take the barrel off him.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
You start enjoying the delicious roast chicken with Paimon.
Henri seems as if he is about to drool, but he holds back the desire to have a share to keep his promise and maintain his dignity.
However, seeing Henri trying really hard to look unaffected, Paimon offers to share the roast chicken with Henri.
The chicken is crispy on the outside and gives out an irresistible oily aroma. Yum yum!

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Freedom! Ahhh, the sweet taste of freedom! Though not as satisfying as roast chicken is, freedom sure is sweet!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...So, what does the board that you are holding stand for?

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Hm? Oh, this. It represents protest, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Against what?

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Hmm... How should I put this... Th—They are the ones who buried me. They did it to stop me from working hard, which is why I want to protest!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, why do they want you to stop working hard?

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Can you keep a secret?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! Your secrets are safe with Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Then yours are safe with me, too. But I'm afraid I can't tell.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Are you making fun of Paimon!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's talk about something else, then...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... What's with the barrel you were wearing? Is that a form of protest as well?

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Huh? That I don't know... Before they buried me, they put this barrel on me — a deed born of their twisted tastes, I'll wager.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And why did you end up buried by them?

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Because they are terrible, terrible people! They just grabbed me for no reason at all and buried me in the sand! They wanted me dead!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No reason at all, huh? Really?

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: O—Of course! Didn't you see? I was literally buried in the sand!

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: If they didn't want me dead, why else would they do it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hmmm... That makes sense... {NICKNAME}, what do you think?

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: ...What? So they didn't intend to kill me at all!

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: *sigh* You guys are really observant. That's right. I was the one who broke the machine!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But why did you break the machine?

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Hmph, why indeed! Because...

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: A long time ago, I lived a poor and miserable life. I was really depressed. Then, I met a guy who gave me a healthy drink that lifted my spirits.

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: He was really kind to me. So I wanted to pay him back for his kindness. One day, I had my chance. He introduced me to some very rich people and asked me to help them.

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: All I did was menial work, such as collecting mechanical parts that belonged to the Fontaine Research Institute. The rich people paid me a pretty sum for those chores.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, sounds pretty awesome.

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Right? This time, they asked me to find this strange machine, take the core out, and deliver the core to them. I can both repay my bro and make some money. I've gotta give my all!

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: But, those terrible people... Perhaps they hated seeing me working hard to change my life for the better. They interfered with my work and warned me against delivering the— umm, precision components to my employers!

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: But I wouldn't let them win! I took the job, and protested against their behavior!

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: And as a result, like you said, I was taught a lesson...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Poor you... But is this job of yours really so well-paid?

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Of course. This is one of the reasons why I didn't want to tell you why I'm protesting. However, since you saved my life...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not as much as saving your life, I mean...

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: ...I also thought that since you two are really observant, I might as well just tell you the truth. You can see it as a collaboration.

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Such strange machines have been deployed above ground and underwater. It's easy to spot such machines — they all produce a peculiar light around them.

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Handle it for me and bring me the specific core inside it. There should be <color=#00E1FFFF>seven</color> in total. After it's done, we'll split the earnings fifty-fifty. Deal?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmmm, but what do these machines do?

response.speaker: Henri
response.text: They destroy the environment. These machines are evil stuff.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Destroy how?

response.speaker: Henri
response.text: How am I going to know? I'm not a member of the Fontaine Research Institute. Anomalies have already occurred, so it has to be hazardous to the environment!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... That sounds reasonable. Every time we see any supernatural environment during our adventure, there's bound to be some trouble that we have to deal with...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, why don't we help Henri?

response.speaker: Henri
response.text: Haha, great! It's settled then! <color=#00E1FFFF>Bring me seven cores</color>, let's become rich together!

choices.text: I take 70% of the earnings and 20% must be paid in advance.

response.speaker: Henri
response.text: Ugh, fine. But I really can't give it to you in advance. I'm still waiting for everything to be done so that I can get paid!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmmm, but what do these machines do?

dialogues.speaker: Henri
dialogues.text: Don't look so wary! This is the latest beauty trend!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those two are pretty strange...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: No, that can't be it...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: ...How do you even manage to bury yourself like that?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The latest beauty fad and a very weird attitude... But why did he have to scream and shout then?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: They are obviously not taking a walk.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Almost ate Henri's head or the roast chicken!

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The skin is grilled to perfection, fragrant and crispy! The sizzling fat inside is releasing a thousand aromatic compounds that speak of tenderness that melts in the mouth! It looks delicious!

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Did he shout so that people other than us could hear him? Speaking of such people, they are probably...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Henri is afraid of asking for our help because he is scared of the walker duo. So the reason why the walker duo makes Henri scared is...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: ...They were the ones who buried Henri.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: I see. Henri wanted to lure the crabs with the roast chicken.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: I see. Henri tried to bury the roast chicken with his shovel but ended up getting buried by crabs.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: A machine with an unclear purpose. Seems like it's no longer functioning. Is it related to the situation here?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The barrel that the walker duo put around Henri's chest before he was buried.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Almost ate Henri's head or the roast chicken!

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The chicken is crispy on the outside and gives out an irresistible oily aroma. Yum yum!

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Under such circumstances, the barrel prevents the sand from applying pressure to the chest so that Henri would not be suffocated. Which is to say, the walker duo did not want to kill him. So their true intention was...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: But Henri was buried, so he couldn't eat it. Though it feels kinda weird, the roast chicken was placed in front of him because...?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: They mentioned "lesson" before leaving. Seems like they wanted to teach Henri a "lesson" by burying him in the sand and letting him see the roast chicken that he couldn't reach. But why?

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: ...Judging from the clues from the scene, the reason could only be this.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Yes, I see. The walker duo wanted to use Henri to attract crabs.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: If it were Paimon, she might've fallen for that.
